label: LOCAL ENGINEERING DRILL - one shared host, single replica of every service, not HA, not a monthly SLA, not candidate-bound acceptance
worktree: dirty (this drill's tooling changes; other sessions committed to the same branch during the run)

host.load_generator: node v22.22.0 on the same host (not a separate calibrated generator)

environment.co_tenancy: Another agent ran PostgreSQL/Supabase drill containers on the same Docker host during the knee series A/B and the first part of the soak; it had stopped by the post-soak knee series C and lock A/B. Host CPU was not reserved for this drill.

images.functions: supabase/edge-runtime:v1.77.4@sha256:ad45164b7548bf5820ed7be714789c17ac2865edce79a09cfb4c3756c3d365a8 (kit pin), upstream self-hosted main router (150 MB / 60 s per worker)
images.gateway: node:24.21.0-alpine3.24 minimal reverse proxy standing in for the kit's Envoy route table (/functions/v1, /rest/v1)

stack.kind: minimal subset of the self-hosted Compose kit, one replica each, one Docker bridge network
services: functions (edge runtime with supabase/functions copied in, as deployment-prepare does)
not_included: GoTrue (auth schema stubbed as the repository's PostgreSQL fixture tests do)
stack.migrations: 181 canonical migrations at drill start applied in order to a fresh database
stack.signing: Ed25519 entitlement/policy signing configured (signed policy envelopes and entitlement snapshots on every 200)
stack.tenants: two pilot-admitted tenants (quiet: 1 member key; noisy: owner + 9 member keys), published runtime policy, 50 seats each

workload.soak: 20 rps offered for 10 800 s; quiet tenant 1.818 rps (1 key); noisy tenant 18.18 rps = 10x (5 keys at 2x the quiet key's rate, which exceeds the 1 200 events/min per-subject ingest quota); 10 events per ingest batch
workload.knee: 2 events per ingest batch, quiet 1 key + noisy 10 keys at equal per-key rate, 60-90 s steps
workload.retries: none during the run; ambiguous ingest batches were re-sent once afterwards with the same event ids (durable-queue semantics)

knee.workload: 11 keys (quiet 1 + noisy 10), 2-event ingest batches : policy polls = 3 : 1, 60-90 s per step, request timeout 10 s, max_in_flight 400
knee.interpretation: With the co-tenant active (series B) goodput tracked offered load up to 28 rps and collapsed at 34 rps; on the quiet host (series C) it tracked to 48 rps with p95 rising to 1.8 s and collapsed at 56 rps. Above the knee there is no load shedding: queued work waits on per-tenant locks inside the shared PostgREST pool (PGRST003 pool timeouts), clients time out at 10 s, and with only 10 s between steps (series A) goodput reached 0 and did not recover until the load stopped.

quiet_control.note: quiet tenant alone at its soak rate (1.818 rps, 10-event batches), 600 s, immediately before the soak

bound.derivation: max(2 x control p95 119 ms, control p95 + 150 ms)
bound.steady_state: soak time excluding [inject_start - 5 s, inject_end + 300 s] around each injected fault

soak.fault_observations_runner_note: Computed by the runner before fix D1; the earlier windows absorbed later faults. fault_recovery (ledger-derived, 20 consecutive successes) is authoritative.

lock_fix_ab.change: supabase/migrations/20261011000400_tenant_admission_capacity_shared_read_lock.sql: tenant_admission_capacity() takes the tenant advisory lock in SHARED mode; every allocating writer still takes it EXCLUSIVE first
lock_fix_ab.test: scripts/tenant-ga-admission-concurrency-postgres.test.mjs: failed before the change (lock timeout on a concurrent reader), passed after; writers are still excluded
lock_fix_ab.method: same 11-key overload profile, function toggled between the two definitions in place, 60 s cool-down, order old/new/old/new
lock_fix_ab.interpretation: Below the knee (34 rps on the quiet host) no difference. In overload (52 rps) goodput rose from 33.0/31.3 to 42.5/37.8 HTTP 200/s and the error ratio fell from 24-28% to 9-16% (two runs per arm, same host, same data). The quiet tenant still failed 7.5-15.9% in overload: the change reduces but does not remove cross-tenant interference above the knee.

findings.title: Load runner stretched an earlier fault window's recovery across later faults
findings.detail: faultObservations() took the last failure over the whole remaining run, so in a multi-fault soak the first window's estimated_rto_ms included every later fault (6 675 s for a 15 s DB restart). The last failure is now taken inside the window; the confirming successes may complete after the window, and a later failure before confirmation leaves the window not_recovered.
findings.test: scripts/load-test.test.mjs 'a later fault does not stretch the recovery time of an earlier fault window' (failed before: 1 703 ms, passes after)

findings.title: Per-tenant exclusive lock in the read-only admission check held shared PostgREST pool slots
findings.detail: Every ingest took the tenant's exclusive advisory lock three times (registration, admission read, event seat trigger). Waiters hold PostgREST connections, so one tenant's backlog exhausts the 10-connection pool and the other tenant times out. The admission read now takes the shared lock; registration and the event seat trigger remain exclusive by design (seat allocation, event-id ownership).

findings.title: Congestion collapse above the knee, no admission control
findings.detail: Abandoned requests keep consuming the edge worker and pool after the client's 10 s timeout; goodput falls towards zero instead of plateauing. Needs a per-tenant in-flight cap or lock_timeout-based shedding at the edge/DB boundary and a pool/gateway timeout budget. Not changed here: it is a product decision about which tenant's requests to shed.

findings.title: DB network partition produces 10 s client hangs and ~30 s recovery after heal
findings.detail: During a 30 s partition PostgREST requests block on dead pooled connections (no fast 503); after the network returned, success resumed 29.7-30.3 s later. No loss or duplication. Dead-peer detection (libpq keepalives / tcp_user_timeout on PGRST_DB_URI) and a request deadline would bound it; not changed (no target was agreed).

findings.title: Edge runtime memory grows then plateaus
findings.detail: functions container RSS 651 MiB at start, ~1.0-1.1 GiB after 30-60 min, 1.12 GiB at 3 h (dropped to 0.85 GiB after the edge restart). No OOM. A plateau over 3 h is not proof of no leak over days.

findings.title: Fixed-window per-subject quota produces 429 bursts at each minute boundary
findings.detail: Noisy keys exhaust 1 200 events/min within the first ~40 s of each window; the quiet tenant saw zero 429s and no latency change from the bursts.

findings.title: Unexplained 60 s slowdown at soak t=600-660 s
findings.detail: Both tenants' p95 rose to ~5 s with 7/10 pool connections active, no injected fault, offered load constant, co-tenant containers active on the host. Not attributed.

isolation_result.scope: At 20 rps offered (about 40% of the quiet-host knee) the quiet tenant stayed within the pre-declared bound while the noisy tenant ran at 10x and was quota-limited (19.8% HTTP 429). It does NOT hold above the knee: see knee and lock_fix_ab.

artefact_hashes_note: Raw ledger/stats/result files were not retained in the repository (about 210 MB); hashes identify the local copies this summary was derived from.
